title: Split formatted markdown strings with unicode support.
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

Continuation of https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/pull/4416

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

This will handle graphemes using `Intl.Segmenter` if available. (Not available in FF)
It also handles lines word by word instead of per character. So performance should be better as we are doing a lot less DOM operations. 

### :clipboard: Tasks

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
It might be worth adding a comment here that this function may return different results depending on the environment/locale.

I think `Intl.Segmenter(undefined)` will use the default locale, which might be `en-US` on one browser, and something else on another browser.

From [**Why should we pass a locale and options bag for grapheme boundaries? Isn't there just one way to do it?**](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-intl-segmenter#why-should-we-pass-a-locale-and-options-bag-for-grapheme-boundaries-isnt-there-just-one-way-to-do-it), it sounds like `Intl.Segmenter` might start returning different results for some Indic languages like Bengali (e.g. `bn-IN` locale).

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests adding a comment about locale-dependent behavior and potential differences across environments.
